questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures do not pass through both greater and lesser sciatic foramens?
questions.explanation:
The tendon of the obturator internus muscle passes only through the lesser sciatic foramen.

Structures passing through both the greater and lesser sciatic foramina are the pudendal nerve, internal pudendal vessels, and nerve to obturator internus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the following structures are derived from the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle except:
questions.explanation:
Linea semilunaris is derived from the aponeurosis of the internal oblique muscle.

Pectineal ligament, inguinal ligament and lacunar ligament are derived from the external oblique aponeurosis.
questions.structuredExplanationText:

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following muscles does not form the floor of the femoral triangle?
questions.explanation:
Psoas major forms the floor of the femoral triangle, not psoas minor.

The femoral triangle is an intermuscular space in the anteromedial aspect of the thigh. Its lateral boundary is the medial margin of sartorius, its medial boundary the medial margin of adductor longus, and its floor from lateral to medial is formed by iliacus, psoas major, pectineus and adductor longus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following forms the lateral boundary of the femoral triangle?
questions.explanation: The lateral boundary of the femoral triangle is formed by the medial margin of the sartorius. Its medial boundary is formed by the medial margin of adductor longus.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The lateral boundary of the femoral triangle is formed by the medial margin of the sartorius. Its medial boundary is formed by the medial margin of adductor longus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A resident was inserting a central venous line through the femoral vein. He accidentally injured the structure medial to the femoral vein, within the femoral sheath. Which structure is likely to be injured?
questions.explanation:
The lymphatic vessels lie medial to the femoral vein and are likely to be injured in this case.

The femoral sheath is the funnel-shaped prolongation of the fascia containing femoral vessels. It is divided into three compartments by intervening septa: lateral compartment contains femoral artery, intermediate compartment contains femoral vein, and the medial compartment (femoral canal) contains lymphatic vessels, areolar tissue and the lymph node of Cloquet.

The empty space in the femoral canal allows distension of the adjacent femoral vein with increased venous return or increased intra-abdominal pressure.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient underwent an aortic valve replacement surgery through the femoral artery. Post-operatively, he complains of groin pain radiating down the anteromedial thigh. Which of the following is true regarding the nerve injured?

options.text: It lies medial to the femoral artery
It is not a content of the femoral sheath
The nerve injured is the sciatic nerve
It arises from the anterior cords of the lumbar plexus

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not a content of the femoral sheath
questions.explanation:
The nerve injured is the femoral nerve. The femoral nerve is not a content of the femoral sheath.

The femoral nerve lies lateral to the femoral artery. The source contrasts this with sciatic nerve injury, which can occur after misplaced intramuscular gluteal injection and may cause sensory loss over the outer ankle/heel and foot drop.

The nerve injured is the femoral nerve. The femoral nerve is not a content of the femoral sheath.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A middle aged man is found to have a globular swelling below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. A diagnosis of femoral hernia is made. Which structure forms the posterior border of the ring the hernia passes through?
questions.explanation:
A femoral hernia passes through the femoral ring proximally. The posterior border of the femoral ring is the pectineal ligament.

Relations of the femoral ring: anteriorly inguinal ligament; posteriorly pectineal ligament, superior pubic ramus and pectineus; medially lacunar ligament; laterally femoral vein.
questions.structuredExplanationText:
A femoral hernia passes through the femoral ring proximally. The posterior border of the femoral ring is the pectineal ligament.

Relations of the femoral ring: anteriorly inguinal ligament; posteriorly pectineal ligament, superior pubic ramus and pectineus; medially lacunar ligament; laterally femoral vein.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An adolescent is crossing the road while playing loud music on his headphones. He is struck by a car and rushed to the emergency room. The physicians noticed a distal femur fracture with vascular compromise. Intraoperatively, the femoral vessels are found to be injured at the adductor hiatus. Which muscle is likely to be involved in this injury?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the femoral vessels are injured at the adductor hiatus. The adductor hiatus is an opening in the tendon of adductor magnus; hence the muscle likely involved is adductor magnus.

Clinical relevance: the adductor part of adductor magnus attaches to the distal femur. Distal femur fractures may cause femoral artery injury and impair blood supply to the lower leg.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The hunter's canal lies beneath which muscle?
questions.explanation: Hunter's canal lies beneath the sartorius muscle. It is also called the subsartorial or adductor canal and is a triangular intermuscular tunnel occupying the lower two-thirds of the medial thigh.
questions.structuredExplanationText: Hunter's canal lies beneath the sartorius muscle. It is also called the subsartorial or adductor canal and is a triangular intermuscular tunnel occupying the lower two-thirds of the medial thigh.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 40 year old basketball player who sustained an ACL tear is being posted for ACL reconstruction surgery. The anesthetist plans an adductor canal block for the procedure. Which of the following structures is least likely to encounter while giving the block?
questions.explanation:
The femoral nerve is least likely to be encountered while giving an adductor canal block. The adductor canal does not contain the femoral nerve.

Contents of the adductor canal include the saphenous nerve, nerve to vastus medialis, femoral artery, descending genicular artery, femoral vein and deep lymphatic vessels.

The femoral nerve is least likely to be encountered while giving an adductor canal block. The adductor canal does not contain the femoral nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct relationship with regards to the saphenous nerve in the adductor canal?
questions.explanation: The saphenous nerve is anterior to the femoral artery in the adductor canal.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The saphenous nerve is anterior to the femoral artery in the adductor canal.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient presents with a chronic ulcer in the popliteal fossa. The surgeon plans to make a musculocutaneous flap using a muscle from the superolateral boundary of the fossa. Which muscle is to be used for the flap?
questions.explanation:
The surgeon should use the biceps femoris muscle for a superolateral popliteal-fossa flap because biceps femoris forms the superolateral border of the popliteal fossa.

The popliteal fossa is a diamond-shaped region posterior to the knee.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is not a content of the popliteal fossa?
questions.explanation:
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is not a content of the popliteal fossa. It arises from the ventral rami of L2 and L3 and supplies the skin of the anterolateral thigh.

Contents of the popliteal fossa listed by the source include popliteal artery and branches; popliteal vein and tributaries; tibial nerve; common fibular (peroneal) nerve; short saphenous vein; posterior femoral cutaneous nerve; articular branch of obturator nerve; medial and lateral sural cutaneous nerves; lymph nodes; fat; and bursae.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following bones form the anterior pillar of the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot?

options.text: Talus, navicular, 3 cuneiform and 1st, 2nd and 3rd metatarsal

questions.explanation: The anterior pillar of the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot is formed by the 4th and 5th metatarsals.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The anterior pillar of the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot is formed by the 4th and 5th metatarsals.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The keystone of the medial longitudinal arch is formed by _____.
questions.explanation: The keystone (summit) of the medial longitudinal arch is formed by the talus.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The keystone (summit) of the medial longitudinal arch is formed by the talus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 42-year-old man had trauma to the right foot, following which he complained of difficulty in walking. Examination showed collapse of the medial longitudinal arch. Injury to all of the following structures may cause the given condition except:
questions.explanation:
Peroneus longus maintains the lateral longitudinal arch and not the medial arch.

The muscles, tendons and aponeurosis maintaining the longitudinal arches act as slings, suspending the arches from above, and as tie beams (bowstrings) between anterior and posterior pillars that prevent separation of the pillars.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures does not pass deep to the superior extensor retinacula of foot?
questions.explanation:
The tendon of tibialis posterior does not pass deep to the superior extensor retinaculum of the foot.

Structures passing deep to the superior and inferior extensor retinacula include tibialis anterior tendon, extensor hallucis longus tendon, deep peroneal nerve, extensor digitorum longus tendon and peroneus tertius tendon. The anterior tibial vessels pass deep to the superior retinaculum and continue as dorsalis pedis deep to the inferior retinaculum.

The tendon of tibialis posterior passes deep to the flexor retinaculum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false about the inferior extensor retinaculum of the foot?

options.text: The upper band is attached to the lower end of the fibula
The lower band is attached to the deep fascia of sole
Laterally it is attached to calcaneum

questions.correctAnswerText: The upper band is attached to the lower end of the fibula
questions.explanation:
The upper band is attached to the medial malleolus of the tibia and not to the fibula.

The inferior extensor retinaculum is a Y-shaped band lying anterior to the ankle joint. The stem of the Y is at the lateral end attached to the upper surface of calcaneus; the limbs lie medially, with the proximal limb attaching to the medial malleolus and the distal limb blending with the plantar aponeurosis.

Structures passing deep include peroneus tertius, extensor digitorum longus, extensor hallucis longus, tibialis anterior, anterior tibial vessels/dorsalis pedis, and deep peroneal nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is the most medial structure passing through the canals in the flexor retinaculum of the foot?
questions.explanation:
Tibialis posterior tendon is the most medial structure passing through the canals in the flexor retinaculum of the foot.

The flexor retinaculum converts grooves on the tibia and calcaneus into canals. From medial to lateral the structures are: tibialis posterior tendon, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve, and flexor hallucis longus tendon.
